discovery: Direct observation of the electron-scale physics of magnetic reconnection in space plasmas

nominees.name: James L. Burch
nominees.affiliation: Southwest Research Institute, San Antonio, USA

nominees.name: Tai D. Phan
nominees.affiliation: Space Sciences Laboratory, University of California, Berkeley, USA

motivation: Magnetic reconnection converts magnetic energy into particle energy throughout the universe, from laboratory fusion devices to solar flares and Earth's magnetosphere, yet its decisive physics occurs at electron scales that were never resolved. Burch and Torbert led NASA's Magnetospheric Multiscale mission, whose four-spacecraft constellation and unprecedented time resolution made the first direct measurements inside the electron diffusion region (Science 2016, 2018), revealing how electrons decouple from the magnetic field and how the frozen-in condition breaks. Phan's observations established reconnection in turbulent magnetosheath plasma, including electron-only reconnection (Nature 2018), showing that reconnection dissipates turbulence at the smallest scales. Together they turned a fundamental plasma process, inferred for seventy years, into a measured phenomenon. This work transformed our understanding of how solar wind energy drives space weather and provides essential benchmarks for kinetic simulations of astrophysical and laboratory plasmas.
